extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors of classical Euclidean geometry (readers of Euclid's Elements)
extracted.subtask_description: Book XI of Euclid's Elements: definitions and propositions about solids, planes, perpendicularity, parallelism, and basic constructions (perpendiculars/erections). Contains precise definitions and theorem statements with accompanying proofs/constructive methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition I — Solid
rubrics_metrics.description: A SOLID is that which hath length, breadth, and thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic ontological definition establishing what is meant by a solid in Euclidean geometry; used as primitive term for subsequent propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition II — Superficies
rubrics_metrics.description: That which bounds a solid is a superficies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the boundary (surface) of a solid; foundational vocabulary for solids and their faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition III — Line perpendicular to a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: A straight line is perpendicular or at right angles to a plane, when it makes right angles with every straight line meeting it in that plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the criterion for a line to be perpendicular to a plane (right angle to every line in the plane through the intersection point); used repeatedly in proofs about perpendicularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition IV — Plane perpendicular to a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: A plane is perpendicular to a plane when the straight lines drawn in one of the planes perpendicularly to the common section of the two planes are perpendicular to the other plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines perpendicularity of planes via perpendiculars to their common intersection line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition V — Inclination of a line to a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclination of a straight line to a plane is the acute angle contained by that straight line and another drawn from the point in which the first line meets the plane, to the point in which a perpendicular to the plane drawn from any point of the first line above the plane, meets the same plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise construction of the acute angle measuring how a line 'inclines' to a plane (used to compare inclinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition VI — Inclination of a plane to a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclination of a plane to a plane is the acute angle contained by two straight lines drawn from any the same point of their common section at right angles to it, one upon one plane, and the other upon the other plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines plane-to-plane angle by measuring between two normals drawn in each plane from a point on their common line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition VII — Same or like inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: Two planes are said to have the same, or a like inclination to one another, which two other planes have, when the said angles of inclination are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a notion of equality of inclinations for comparing pairs of planes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition VIII — Parallel planes
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel planes are such which do not meet one another though produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard definition of parallelism for planes, analogous to parallel lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition IX — Solid angle
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid angle is that which is made by the meeting of more than two plane angles, which are not in the same plane, in one point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the 3D analogue of a plane angle as meeting of plane angles about a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition X — (omitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tenth definition is omitted (note refers to editorial/notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placeholder noting omission; no substantive geometric criterion here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition (XI) — Similar solid figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar solid figures are such as have all their solid angles equal, each to each, and which are contained by the same number of similar planes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the criterion for similarity of solids: corresponding solid angles equal and faces similar in number and shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XII — Pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: A pyramid is a solid figure contained by planes that are constituted betwixt one plane and one point above it in which they meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines pyramid as planes from a base plane to an apex point; used for naming classes of solids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XIII — Prism
rubrics_metrics.description: A prism is a solid figure contained by plane figures of which two that are opposite are equal, similar, and parallel to one another; and the others parallelograms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes prisms by parallel, similar opposite faces and parallelogram sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XIV — Sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: A sphere is a solid figure described by the revolution of a semicircle about its diameter, which remains unmoved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic definition of sphere via revolution of a semicircle about its diameter (axis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XV — Axis of a sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The axis of a sphere is the fixed straight line about which the semicircle revolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the axis/rotation line for the sphere construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XVI — Centre of a sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The centre of a sphere is the same with that of the semicircle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the central point of symmetry for the sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XVII — Diameter of a sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The diameter of a sphere is any straight line which passes through the centre, and is terminated both ways by the superficies of the sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to circle diameter; used in later propositions relating to perpendiculars and circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XVIII — Cone
rubrics_metrics.description: A cone is a solid figure described by the revolution of a right angled triangle about one of the sides containing the right angle, which side remains fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines cone via rotation of a right triangle; further classifies cones (right-angled, obtuse, acute) by relation of sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XIX — Axis of a cone
rubrics_metrics.description: The axis of a cone is the fixed straight line about which the triangle revolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the generating axis for cones; used for similarity and proportionality of cones and cylinders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XX — Base of a cone
rubrics_metrics.description: The base of a cone is the circle described by that side containing the right angle, which revolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the circular base produced by the rotating side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXI — Cylinder
rubrics_metrics.description: A cylinder is a solid figure described by the revolution of a right angled parallelogram about one of its sides, which remains fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines cylinders analogously to cones via revolution of a parallelogram.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXII — Axis of a cylinder
rubrics_metrics.description: The axis of a cylinder is the fixed straight line about which the parallelogram revolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines central axis of cylinder used in similarity statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXIII — Bases of a cylinder
rubrics_metrics.description: The bases of a cylinder are the circles described by the two revolving opposite sides of the parallelogram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the two circular bases of a cylinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXIV — Similar cones and cylinders
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar cones and cylinders are those which have their axes and the diameters of their bases proportional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives precise proportionality condition for similarity of these solids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXV — Cube
rubrics_metrics.description: A cube is a solid figure contained by six equal squares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard polyhedron definition used for later classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXVI — Tetrahedron
rubrics_metrics.description: A tetrahedron is a solid figure contained by four equal and equilateral triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines regular tetrahedron.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXVII — Octahedron
rubrics_metrics.description: An octahedron is a solid figure contained by eight equal and equilateral triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of regular octahedron for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXVIII — Dodecahedron
rubrics_metrics.description: A dodecahedron is a solid figure contained by twelve equal pentagons which are equilateral and equiangular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines regular dodecahedron (Platonic solid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition XXIX — Icosahedron
rubrics_metrics.description: An icosahedron is a solid figure contained by twenty equal and equilateral triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines regular icosahedron.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition A — Parallelepiped
rubrics_metrics.description: A parallelepiped is a solid figure contained by six quadrilateral figures, whereof every opposite two are parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines parallelepiped (3D analogue of parallelogram) used in volume and parallelism arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition I (Book XI) — One part of a line not in and above a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: One part of a straight line cannot be in a plane and another part above it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: assume part AB in plane and BC above; produce AB in plane to D and rotate a plane through AD to pass through C, yielding two distinct straight lines in the same plane sharing a common segment (contradiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition II — Intersecting lines lie in one plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Two straight lines which cut one another are in one plane, and three straight lines which meet one another are in one plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a plane through the common segment and show the third point can be included by rotating plane; uses ability to turn planes about a line to include points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition III — Intersection of two planes is a straight line
rubrics_metrics.description: If two planes cut one another, their common section is a straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if common section were not straight, you could draw two distinct straight lines between the same endpoints, forming an included area — impossible; hence common section must be a straight line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition IV — Line perpendicular to two lines is perpendicular to their plane
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line stand at right angles to each of two straight lines in the point of their intersection, it shall also be at right angles to the plane which passes through them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs equal segments and uses congruent triangles to show the given line makes right angles with every line in the plane through the intersection, hence is perpendicular to the plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition V — Three lines through a point with a common perpendicular lie in one plane
rubrics_metrics.description: If three straight lines meet all in one point, and a straight line stands at right angles to each of them in that point; these three straight lines are in one and the same plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument by contradiction: assume one line lies above the plane of the other two, derive impossible equal-right-angle relations; conclude all three are coplanar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VI — Two lines perpendicular to same plane are parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines be at right angles to the same plane, they shall be parallel to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof places perpendiculars meeting the plane and constructs congruent right triangles to show corresponding bases equal and angles right, concluding parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VII — Segment joining points on parallel lines is coplanar with them
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines be parallel, the straight line drawn from any point in the one to any point in the other is in the same plane with the parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: if the connector were out of the plane, two distinct straight lines would connect same points in different planes, creating impossible enclosed space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VIII — Parallel line perpendicular to plane implies the other is also perpendicular
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines be parallel, and one of them is at right angles to a plane, the other also shall be at right angles to the same plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs perpendiculars in the plane and uses parallels and congruent triangles to transfer right-angle property to the other line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition IX — Lines parallel to same line (off-plane) are parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: Two straight lines which are each of them parallel to the same straight line, and not in the same plane with it, are parallel to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs perpendiculars in planes containing the given line and each candidate, shows both are perpendicular to a common plane and hence parallel to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition X — Equal angles from corresponding parallel pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines meeting one another be parallel to two others that meet one another, and are not in the same plane with the first two, the first two and the other two shall contain equal angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct equal-length segments and parallellisms to reduce to comparing corresponding bases; uses prior results about parallels and planar relations to deduce angle equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XI (Problem) — Drop perpendicular from point above plane
rubrics_metrics.description: To draw a straight line perpendicular to a plane, from a given point above it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: draw any line in the plane, drop a perpendicular from the given point to that line; using further perpendicular constructions and parallels, construct the required perpendicular to the plane (full constructive steps given in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XII (Problem) — Erect perpendicular from point in plane
rubrics_metrics.description: To erect a straight line at right angles to a given plane, from a point given in the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take a point above the plane, drop perpendicular to plane, draw through given point a line parallel to that perpendicular; parallel to a perpendicular to the plane is itself perpendicular to the plane — yields the erected perpendicular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XIII — Uniqueness of perpendicular from a point
rubrics_metrics.description: From the same point in a given plane, there cannot be two straight lines at right angles to the plane, upon the same side of it; and there can be but one perpendicular to a plane from a point above the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses plane intersections and right-angle contradictions to show two distinct perpendiculars would produce impossible equal-right-angle triangle properties or parallel contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XIV — Planes perpendicular to same line are parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: Planes to which the same straight line is perpendicular, are parallel to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: assume two such planes meet; take a point on their intersection and join to the perpendicular line's points to derive impossible triangle with two right angles summing to 180°, thus planes cannot meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XV — Parallelism of planes determined by parallel line pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines meeting one another be parallel to two straight lines which meet one another, but are not in the same plane with the first two; the plane which passes through these is parallel to the plane passing through the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a perpendicular to one plane, then parallels to the given lines to show a common perpendicular to both planes exists; planes sharing a common perpendicular are parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XVI — Sections of parallel planes by a plane are parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: If two parallel planes be cut by another plane, their common sections with it are parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard result: intersection lines of the cutting plane with each of the parallel planes are themselves parallel; proof uses properties of parallel planes and lines.
